historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 management guidance (total revenue +5-6%) and the pre-Paycor organic record (FY2019-FY2024 revenue CAGR 7.0% including the Oasis deal, ~5-6% organic); NOT equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.3%/4.8%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (9.2%/9.9%) and EPS (4.3%/9.9%) CAGRs. Paychex distributes ~80-100% of net income as dividends plus buybacks ($4.43 DPS vs $4.90 EPS in FY2026, plus $611M of repurchases), so book value is not the compounding base and the equity CAGR is not a usable growth proxy. The FY2023-FY2026 window is also distorted by the ~$4.1B Paycor acquisition (debt-funded, April 2025), which inflates revenue and FCF CAGRs while EPS CAGR is depressed by the new interest expense and intangible amortization.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income never stripped because net cash never exceeded 1x FCF): FY2021 1,089.4; FY2022 1,403.1; FY2023 1,500.6; FY2024 1,675.2; FY2025 1,597.3; FY2026 2,225.7. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.1pp of each other because SBC is only ~1.5% of revenue and has not outgrown cash flow. Both are inflated by (a) Paycor consolidation from April 2025 and (b) the FY2026 cash-tax shelter (~$240M below a normalized 24% rate); on a normalized unlevered basis FY2026 owner FCF is ~$2.05-2.1B, not $2.23B.

scenario_narratives.base: Paychex compounds as a mature, highly recurring processor: FY2027 revenue grows at the 5-6% guided midpoint with Paycor now organic, PEO & Insurance outgrows Management Solutions, and growth decays to 3% over the decade as small-business formation normalises. Adjusted operating margin reaches the guided ~44% in FY2027 and a further ~0.7pp from synergies and AI service automation, then plateaus. The cash-tax shelter of FY2026 normalises to 24% by year 3. Nothing in the base case requires the mid-market bet to succeed beyond holding Paycor's existing book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Paycor platform turns Paychex into a credible mid-market HCM competitor, PEO keeps growing at low-double digits, and float income holds up as rates stay higher for longer. Growth runs at 6.5-7% for three years and cost synergies plus agentic AI push the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 50%. This is the multi-year story the pre-2026 multiple (25-30x FCF) was pricing.
scenario_narratives.bear: Three headwinds already visible in Q1 FY2027 persist: core Management Solutions growth decelerates to ~3% as SaaS-native entrants take the smallest clients and SMB hiring stalls; rate cuts erode the near-100%-margin float income on client funds; and running three parallel platforms keeps integration cost in the P&L. Growth settles at 2.5%, margins drift ~1.3pp below FY2026, and the terminal multiple compresses to 18x. The post-Paycor debt ($4.56B) does not threaten solvency but removes the option to buy growth again.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Paychex as a mature compounder on fully SBC-expensed, unlevered owner FCF built from components, with the FY2026 cash-tax shelter and the non-deductible Paycor amortization both normalised out so neither the tax rate nor the D&A tax shield flatters the flows. Growth is anchored to management's FY2027 guidance and the pre-Paycor organic record, not to acquisition-inflated CAGRs or to an equity CAGR that is meaningless for a company paying out nearly all of its earnings. Scenarios differ by drivers (growth, margin, terminal growth and cap), never by WACC, so risk is charged exactly once, in the weights.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries the majority of enterprise value at an 8% WACC; each 0.5pp of WACC moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid).
Float income on funds held for clients is ~3% of revenue at near-100% margin; a faster or deeper rate-cutting cycle than the bear case assumes would take base-case margins below the modelled plateau.
Paycor integration: cost synergies and cross-sell are assumed in the base margin ramp; client attrition across three platforms would show up first in Management Solutions growth.

SBC is small (~1.5% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow; the valuation is not sensitive to the SBC regime, but it IS sensitive to the cash-tax normalisation (FY2026's 13.4% cash rate must not be read as repeatable).
Net debt is taken at the seasonal cash low (31 Aug); the 31 May balance sheet would add ~$1.4/share.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 85.45-129.24
data_sources.financials: research/PAYX/Reports/PAYX_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL path, FY2007-FY2026) for history; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 723531) for the Q1 FY2027 10-Q anchors filed 2026-09-24: diluted shares, debt, cash, buybacks, SBC, cash taxes, intangible amortization and depreciation
data_sources.qualitative: research/PAYX/Reports/PAYX_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): FY2027 guidance as of the Q1 FY2027 release 2026-09-23, bull/bear axes, Paycor acquisition detail

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for Q1 FY2027 (Jun-Aug 2026) from the 10-Q filed 2026-09-24, 356.6M; cover-page basic count 355.98M at 2026-08-31. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). FY2026 buybacks of $611M funded the flat count; Q1 FY2027 repurchased nothing.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation $96.1M, XBRL). Paychex tags no separate net-share-settlement withholding line, and publishes no combined equity-award figure, so the add-back is used as is; any withholding cost is unquantified and small relative to $2.3B of FCF.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10-year UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 for a low-volatility recurring-revenue processor gives a cost of equity ~8.7%; post-Paycor debt of $4.56B (senior notes, ~5.2% pre-tax, ~4.0% after tax) is ~11% of a ~$40B enterprise value, so WACC rounds to 8.0%. Held identical across scenarios: risk is carried in the driver paths and the weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases (offices): lease cost is inside operating expenses and therefore already inside the EBITDA margin path. Lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing table, 'operating company' row). Paychex is an asset-light recurring-fee payroll/HCM/PEO processor; its value is a stream of free cash flow, so the house engine applies without the non-US/cyclical adaptations. CASH AND FUNDS HELD FOR CLIENTS: `cash` is corporate cash and equivalents only; the ~$5B+ of funds held for clients is excluded because it is offset one-for-one by client fund obligations, and the interest earned on those funds (~3% of revenue) is operating revenue that stays in the top line. Corporate interest income is small and the company is net debt, so no interest strip is applied (interest_income = 0). CASH TAX: FY2026 cash taxes were $310.3M against $550.8M of tax expense (13.4% cash rate vs 23.8% GAAP), the OBBBA domestic R&D-expensing catch-up; the model ramps the cash rate 21% -> 23% -> 24% rather than carrying the shelter forward. D&A: of FY2026's $442.6M D&A, $299.5M is amortization dominated by acquired Paycor intangibles, which are not tax-deductible (stock acquisition, no basis step-up) and are not replaced by capex; da_pct is therefore set at 3.5% of revenue (depreciation $143M + internal-use software amortization), not the 6.8% all-in figure, so the tax shield is not overstated by ~$55M/yr. Adjusted operating margin guidance (~44% FY2027 from ~43% FY2026) maps onto a pre-SBC EBITDA margin anchor of 46.8% in FY2026 ((2,953.1 + 96.1) / 6,512). Net debt is at 2026-08-31 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q), a seasonal cash low after the quarterly dividend; using the 2026-05-31 balance sheet instead would add ~$1.4/share. HORIZON: 10 years so that the revenue deceleration from Paycor-inflated growth to a mature mid-single-digit rate is explicit before capitalisation; owner-FCF margin is mature by year 4.

bear.growth_rationale: The Q1 FY2027 Management Solutions print (4%) is the run-rate, not a blip: SMB hiring stalls, Gusto/Rippling keep winning the newest and smallest clients, and Fed cuts take ~1pp off total growth via float income. Growth settles at 2.5%, barely above inflation.
bear.margin_rationale: Float income (near-100% margin) shrinks with rates, pricing concessions to hold small clients, and integration costs on three parallel platforms linger; pre-SBC EBITDA margin drifts back below the pre-Paycor level to 45.5%. Terminal cap 18x for a structurally slower business.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 at the guidance midpoint (5-6%); Paycor is now fully lapped so this is organic. Management Solutions grew 4% in Q1 FY2027 against a 5-6% full-year range while PEO & Insurance grew 12%, so 5.5% assumes the H2 reacceleration management is guiding to. Decays to 3% by year 9 as SMB formation normalises and the mid-market cross-sell matures.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 46.8% in FY2026; guidance implies ~1pp of adjusted operating-margin expansion in FY2027 (43% -> 44%) from Paycor cost synergies and AI-driven service automation, then a further ~0.7pp before plateauing at 48.5%. The plateau is ~2.8pp above the pre-Paycor FY2024 level (45.7%), consistent with synergies landing but not with Paycor's lower-margin mid-market book ever matching legacy Paychex.
base.tax_rationale: Cash rate ramps 21/23/24%: the OBBBA R&D-expensing benefit fades after FY2027 and the GAAP effective rate is ~24%.
base.wc_rationale: Deferred revenue is ~$70M on $6.5B of revenue; billing is per payroll run, so there is no prepaid float to capture. Zero.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of guidance in FY2027, then 7% as the Paycor mid-market platform (Paychex's historic weak spot) takes share from UKG/Paylocity and PEO keeps compounding at low-double digits; ~1-1.5pp above base through year 6.
bull.margin_rationale: Full synergy capture plus agentic-AI service automation lifts the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 50% (adjusted operating margin ~46%), roughly ADP's Employer Services trajectory.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Shifted from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because three independent headwinds are already in the data rather than hypothetical: Management Solutions grew 4% in Q1 FY2027 against 5-6% guidance, the Fed easing cycle directly cuts float income, and the sell-side's September 2026 target cuts reflect visible SMB share loss to Gusto/Rippling. Bull cut to 25% because it requires Paycor mid-market share gains, sustained PEO double-digit growth AND margin expansion to 50% to all land together. No going-concern or covenant risk: the $4.56B of debt is ~1.5x EBITDA.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
